title: Warli painting
summary: Warli painting comes from the Warli communities of Maharashtra and the Gujarat border in western India. Scenes of village life are drawn in white rice paste on red-brown earth walls, using only a circle, a triangle and a line: a person is two triangles joined at their tips below a round head.
howToPlay: Pick white or brown paste and a simple shape from the tray under the wall.
Tap a square to draw the shape there: its twin appears at the mirrored place on the other side of the wall.
Copy the small wall shown above, then press Check.
rules: Every shape you draw is repeated in the mirrored square on the other side of the wall.
A square counts only when its shape and its colour both match the target.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; you can undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: Warli painting belongs to the Warli communities, who live in the hills and coastal strip of Maharashtra and neighbouring Gujarat, and it was traditionally painted by women on the inside walls of village houses. This game draws only everyday scenes: trees, field work and dancers.
credits: Warli painting is the heritage of the Warli communities of Maharashtra and Gujarat, India
